review_notes: I read the whole file and its downstream uses in MayerVietoris.lean, Singular/MayerVietoris/Basic.lean, Relative.lean and CubeComplement.lean. I also read the Mathlib lemmas ContinuousMap.inclusion_comp_inclusion, subtypeVal_comp_inclusion, and TopCat.ofHom_comp and ofHom_id. The one simp lemma in the file, ofHom_inclusion_comp_ofHom_inclusion, is oriented correctly. It is needed because the simp-normal form from ofHom_comp is `ofHom f ≫ ofHom g`, so Mathlib's `inclusion_comp_inclusion` cannot fire on it. I found no cycle or competing rules. The lemmas ofHom_subtypeVal_comp and ofHom_inclusion_comp are rightly not simp: they have no canonical direction and are always used by explicit `rw`. The only gap I found is a missing categorical counterpart of subtypeVal_comp_inclusion. The evidence for it is moderate: no current call site obviously needs it. I could not run Lean, so I did not check simp behaviour experimentally.

findings.declaration: TopCat.ofHom_inclusion_comp_ofHom_inclusion (simp interface of the file; missing companion for inclusion ≫ subtypeVal)
findings.problem: The file makes nested-inclusion composites simp-normalizable, but it has no matching simp lemma for the other composite of the same family, `ofHom (ContinuousMap.inclusion h) ≫ ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal t) = ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal s)`. Mathlib has the bundled-map version `ContinuousMap.subtypeVal_comp_inclusion` as simp, but its LHS is `(subtypeVal t).comp (inclusion h)`. In `TopCat`, simp normalizes with `ofHom_comp` to `ofHom f ≫ ofHom g`, so that lemma never matches the categorical composite. The simp-normal form of `ofHom (inclusion h) ≫ ofHom (subtypeVal t)` is therefore stuck. The pattern is exactly the one the file already fixes for inclusion ≫ inclusion. The `subtypeVal` inclusions are the ones used in `commSq_ofHom_inter` and in the Mayer–Vietoris naturality proofs.
findings.proposed_change: Add, next to `ofHom_inclusion_comp_ofHom_inclusion`, a lemma such as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)] lemma ofHom_inclusion_comp_ofHom_subtypeVal {α : Type u} [TopologicalSpace α] {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : ofHom (ContinuousMap.inclusion h) ≫ ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal t) = ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal s)`. The proof is `rfl`, or `rw [← ofHom_comp, ContinuousMap.subtypeVal_comp_inclusion]`. The orientation is right: it replaces two morphisms by one, so it terminates and does not conflict with `ofHom_comp`. Do not mark `ofHom_subtypeVal_comp` or `ofHom_inclusion_comp` as simp, since they have no canonical direction.
findings.benefit: Composites of an inclusion followed by an ambient subtype inclusion reduce to a single `subtypeVal` under `simp` or `simp_rw`. Callers then do not need hand-written `rfl` or `change` steps. This is the same convenience Mathlib already provides at the `ContinuousMap` level, now available at the `TopCat` level, and the `reassoc` form handles longer composites in functor and homology proofs.

evidence.excerpt: ofHom (g.comp f) = ofHom f ≫ ofHom g
